run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T22:00:54Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by a burst of failed frontend requests between about 22:04 and 22:11 UTC that were caused by the ad service being unreachable. frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' ERROR span rates rose from ~0/s to ~1.0/s (peak 1.037/s at 2026-11-17T22:08:54Z) and returned to baseline after ~22:15:54Z (evidence 07563175-bb1d-40dd-afc8-a656d58c3efa-t0:3742c60b-756d-4359-9d7b-64668ffc4ec9). The frontend's own errors are HTTP 500 spans on GET /api/data and on its client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, whose error detail is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' - 100.70.197.56 is the ClusterIP of Service ad (evidence 94d12ec1-e14e-4ece-8511-003e0f3322f5-t0:20590a25-3f39-4216-aece-27cfd478c816, b16c1577-367d-4efb-a9c5-e04f484b99a1-t0:69258754-131c-42d6-b636-a6f6a4aeb68c). Deployment ad was rolled out at 22:02:14Z with an unchanged pod template (only annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:02:14Z differs); the new ad container was created and started at 22:02:16Z but its own logs show 'Ad service starting.' only at 22:07:03Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 22:08:59Z, with ad-side GetAds span traffic at zero for the 22:04-22:11 windows (evidence b9db89c1-95c9-48c0-9afb-12a869fffbd2-t0:a1fd894b-d786-47b1-984d-d6374bf49816, 69050919-2c96-4aa1-967f-f48637ec7fdd-t0:710ef0d5-a604-4504-97c6-55826ac339b4, 8adfa63f-fb25-44b6-b55b-1fe20d4571d4-t0:e9545fbb-0556-4c1c-bea1-b7abd1e4337c, ea55c5b8-0b25-4c7a-8fc9-18e04fb04e7f-t0:6ed75db8-49da-483b-bb18-2475ea6e5af9). The only switched-on fault-injection setting found in the namespace is ConfigMap flagd-config's 'adFailure' flag (defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service'), and it names the very service that was restarted with an unchanged pod template; it is therefore reported as the likely origin object, but the declared fault behaviour itself (ad returning application errors) was not observed - what was observed was a transport-level connection refusal while the new ad container had not yet bound port 8080 - and the time the flag was changed cannot be established (no change-history integration), so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own ERROR span rate rose during the incident: 'ingress' ERROR went from 0/s (21:40:54-21:51:54Z) to 0.0148/s at 22:00:54Z, peaked at 1.037/s at 22:08:54Z and fell back to ~0.0148/s by 22:15:54Z; the 'router frontend egress' ERROR series followed the same shape (0 -> 1.011/s at 22:08:54Z -> 0/s by 22:15:54Z).
At 22:00:54Z frontend-proxy served 12.65 spans/s with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 0.0148 spans/s with STATUS_CODE_ERROR on 'ingress', and 12.65/s UNSET with 0/s ERROR on 'router frontend egress'.

The frontend service's own ERROR spans during the incident are on operation 'GET /api/data' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' (error rate 0 at 21:55-22:03Z, peaking 1.0148/s at 22:10:00Z) and on the client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (same shape, peaking 1.0148/s at 22:10:00Z), plus a small 'tcp.connect' error rate (max 0.048/s); GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and the cart/checkout client spans show 0 error rate.

Sampled frontend error spans (22:09:22Z, trace df313cdaac0af99f3c8290c54dfde1a2) record GET 500 with otel.status_code ERROR, and the nested 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' span carries rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'; the /api/data route span carries the same exception message.
Service ad in namespace otel-demo is a ClusterIP service with clusterIP 100.70.197.56 and port 8080 (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad), i.e. the exact address in the frontend's ECONNREFUSED error.

The ad service stopped serving GetAds: its 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' UNSET span rate fell from ~1.02/s at 22:01Z to 0.2/s (22:07:00Z), 0.0037/s (22:08:00Z) and 0 at 22:09:00, 22:10:00 and 22:11:00Z, recovering to 0.296/s at 22:12:00Z; 'getAdsByCategory' and 'getRandomAds' show the same collapse.

ad emitted no ERROR-status spans of its own in this window: the only ad ERROR series are 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' at 0.0037/s from 21:58:00Z to 22:02:00Z, which then reads 0, while 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' ERROR/UNSET read 0 throughout.

Deployment ad in otel-demo was rolled out at 22:02:14Z: ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 'Created pod: ad-785b4464f5-9bshh' and scaled up 0->1, the old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc got 'Killing - Stopping container ad' at 22:02:16Z, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 was deleted/scaled down 1->0, and the new pod was Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started between 22:02:14Z and 22:02:16Z (all Normal events).

The old and new ad ReplicaSet pod templates are identical in image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), env (AD_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_*), containerPort 8080 and resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi), and neither template declares a readinessProbe or livenessProbe; the only difference is the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:02:14Z on ad-785b4464f5.

The new ad container's logs begin with 'Ad service starting.' at 22:07:03.907Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 22:08:59.208Z, and request handling ('Targeted ad request received ...') starts at 22:09:40Z - i.e. the process only began starting ~4m47s and only bound port 8080 ~6m43s after the container was started at 22:02:16Z.

Pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh is Running and Ready with container 'ad' restartCount 0, no previous (terminated) instance and state running startedAt 2026-11-17T22:02:16Z; the ad Service endpoint now points to that pod at 100.96.3.224:8080.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds a flag 'adFailure' with defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service' and state ENABLED, while every other fault flag in the same file (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

Error-span rates of other services in the same window did not show a comparable spike: accounting and payment ERROR series read 0/s at every sampled instant, ad and fraud-detection and recommendation stayed at background 0.0037/s or 0, while frontend rose to 2.53/s (22:05:54Z) - 4.02/s (22:08:54Z).

The alert is caused by this chain: Deployment ad's 22:02:14Z rollout replaced its single pod; the new ad container's process did not bind port 8080 until 22:08:59Z, so callers dialling the ad ClusterIP 100.70.197.56:8080 were refused; frontend's /api/data route propagated gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE to HTTP 500, and frontend-proxy's ingress/egress error rate rose until ad began answering at ~22:09-22:11Z.

Because the pod template contains no readinessProbe, the new ad pod (container ready = running from 22:02:16Z) would have been published as an ad Service endpoint before the application bound port 8080, which is consistent with callers seeing ECONNREFUSED on the ClusterIP rather than an application-level gRPC error.

The switched-on fault-injection setting adFailure ('Fail ad service') in ConfigMap flagd-config is the origin of this incident: it names the ad service, that service was restarted at 22:02:14Z with an unchanged pod template (purely a restartedAt annotation change), and no other object was observed applying a change or fault to the ad workload; the restart and the resulting connection-refused errors are its mechanism and consequences.

The declared effect of adFailure ('Fail ad service') was not observed at the application layer: ad produced no ERROR-status spans and no error log lines during 22:02-22:16Z, and the failures seen by the caller are TCP connection refusals to the Service IP, not RPC status errors returned by the ad process.

An ad container crash, OOMKill or eviction is not supported: the ad container has restartCount 0, no lastState.terminated, state running startedAt 22:02:16Z, and the otel-demo events for ad are only Normal Scheduling/Pulling/Creating/Starting/ScalingReplicaSet entries with no Evicted, OOMKilling, BackOff or Unhealthy event.

The other flagd fault flags (cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak) are all defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, and accounting/payment error-rate series were 0/s while frontend's failing calls are specifically GetAds, so those flags are not the cause of this error spike.

The fraud-detection container's earlier OOMKill (exitCode 137, reason OOMKilled, finishedAt 2026-11-17T21:36:52Z, restartCount 1) is background, not part of this alert: it completed before the frontend error onset (~22:04Z) and fraud-detection's own ERROR series stayed at 0.0037/s or 0 across the window.

Add a readinessProbe (TCP or gRPC on 8080) to the ad container so the pod only enters the ad Service endpoints once the application is listening, and run more than one ad replica so a single rollout does not take the service to zero listeners.

Investigate why the ad process needed ~4m47s before logging 'Ad service starting.' and ~6m43s before binding 8080 under its cpu limit of 50m / request of 10m, and consider raising the ad CPU request/limit before the next rollout.

Confirm with the flagd owner whether adFailure was intentionally left 'on' in ConfigMap flagd-config; if the fault was injected, record when it was set and switch it back to 'off' when the exercise ends (the flag reading is still 'on' while the errors have already stopped).

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule expression, threshold and target metric could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data and a listing with type=alert returned no rules, so the alert's 'current: 2.4555555555555553' value cannot be matched to any observed series.

The alert is reported as starting at 2026-11-17T22:00:54Z, i.e. before the ad rollout (22:02:14Z) and before the main frontend error ramp (first nonzero error bucket 22:03:54Z); what made the rule fire at 22:00:54Z is unexplained.

No change history is available (change_history integration is not integrated in this Run), so who or what enabled flagd's adFailure flag and when it was changed cannot be determined; the flag is 'on' in the object read after the window.
The declared fault itself was not observed: no ad-side application errors or error logs were seen, so the causal link from flagd-config's adFailure flag to the connection refusals remains unverified.

Why the new ad process took ~4m47s to print 'Ad service starting.' is unknown; kube-state-metrics series are not present in this Prometheus (get_metric_names {__name__=~"kube_.*"} and rpc_* both returned no names/values), so container CPU throttling and pod-level resource behaviour could not be checked.

The ad container's log stream starts at 'Ad service starting.' 22:07:03Z; whether anything was written between container start (22:02:16Z) and that line (e.g. a stuck init) is unknown, and there is no previous container instance to read.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in otel-demo returned nothing, so a network-level policy or quota cause can neither be shown nor fully excluded for the incident window.

flagd pod logs could not be read (all containers returned 0 bytes for 21:55-22:16Z), so flagd's own health and flag-serving behaviour during the window is unknown; no flagd service series exist in traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

No error-status series were returned for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote or shipping, which is unknown rather than zero - their error state during the window was not established.
The service ad endpoint object read after the window reflects current state only; the endpoint population between 22:02:16Z and 22:08:59Z was not directly observed.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule (expression, threshold, evaluation window, target metric) from the Prometheus rule files to reconcile the 22:00:54Z start time and the reported value 2.4555.

Check the change/audit trail or GitOps history for ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config and for the deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 change and the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:02:14Z rollout of Deployment ad.
Ask the flagd/demo owner whether the adFailure fault was intentionally injected, and confirm the effective flag value in the flagd UI (port 4000) alongside the ConfigMap.
Add readiness probing and a second ad replica, and re-run the rollout to verify that ad stays in the Service endpoints only while listening.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null).
